say: You start a new task, and git gives you a fresh worktree in a second.
But it starts empty. No dependencies, no dev shell, and none of your local files.
On a big monorepo, getting it ready takes over a minute and gigabytes of disk. And it happens every single time.
Now run five coding agents side by side. That is five minutes of waiting before anyone writes a line.
clove keeps one golden image of your repo, with dependencies installed and the environment warmed. Each worktree is a copy-on-write clone of it.

Under the hood, it leans on what your file system already does well. On macOS, each clone is an APFS disk image, copied whole by a single clonefile call. On Linux, it's a btrfs snapshot, taken in a few milliseconds.
So a new worktree is ready in about a second. Everything is already there, and it takes almost no disk.
When a lockfile changes, only that step runs again.
Use it from the command line, from a full-screen terminal interface, or from the desktop app, on macOS and Linux.
It brings your clones up to date, with Claude resolving the conflicts. It cleans up after merged pull requests. And it teaches your agents to use it.
That's clove. Your worktrees, ready in a second.
